statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSED: Represents nonexistent connections. LISTEN and CLOSED are not associated with any particular DCCP connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: LISTEN: Represents server sockets in the passive listening state. LISTEN and CLOSED are not associated with any particular DCCP connection.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: REQUEST: A client socket enters this state, from CLOSED, after sending a DCCP-Request packet to try to initiate a connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: RESPOND: A server socket enters this state, from LISTEN, after receiving a DCCP-Request from a client.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: PARTOPEN: A client socket enters this state, from REQUEST, after receiving a DCCP-Response from the server. This state represents the third phase of the three-way handshake. The client may send application data in this state, but it MUST include an Acknowledgement Number on all of its packets.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: OPEN: The central data transfer portion of a DCCP connection. Client and server sockets enter this state from PARTOPEN and RESPOND, respectively. Sometimes we speak of SERVER-OPEN and CLIENT-OPEN states, corresponding to the server's OPEN state and the client's OPEN state.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: CLOSEREQ: A server socket enters this state, from SERVER-OPEN, to order the client to close the connection and to hold TIMEWAIT state.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: CLOSING: Server and client sockets can both enter this state to close the connection.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: TIMEWAIT: A server or client socket remains in this state for 2MSL (4 minutes) after the connection has been torn down, to prevent mistakes due to the delivery of old packets. Only one of the endpoints has to enter TIMEWAIT state (the other can enter CLOSED state immediately).

report original DCCP-Request in Data Dropped option as Drop Code 0 Drop Block if data was refused

actions: include Init Cookie in every packet sent from PARTOPEN

actions: set retransmission timer (~200ms) on each transmitted packet
retransmit DCCP-Ack if timer fires and still in PARTOPEN
back off timer on retransmission

actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 2 (Aborted)

actions: immediately generate DCCP-SyncAck
send DCCP-SyncAck (subject to implementation rate limits)

statements.description: Data received during that time SHOULD be rejected and reported using a Data Dropped Drop Block with Drop Code 0, Protocol Constraints (see Section 11.7).

actions: reject received data
report rejection using Data Dropped Drop Block with Drop Code 0 (Protocol Constraints)

statements.subject: connection

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: DCCP implementations generally transition to the CLOSED state after sending a DCCP-Reset packet.

actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 1 Closed

actions: hold TIMEWAIT state for connection

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Scenario 3, step 4: Server moves from TIMEWAIT to CLOSED after 2MSL wait time (4 minutes).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The receiver of a valid DCCP-Reset packet will hold TIMEWAIT state for the connection. The endpoint that receives a valid DCCP-Reset SHOULD hold TIMEWAIT state for the connection.
actions: hold TIMEWAIT state for connection

statements.description: DCCP implementations generally transition to the CLOSED state after sending a DCCP-Reset packet.

statements.description: Only the server can send a DCCP-CloseReq packet or enter the CLOSEREQ state.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Resets sent in the CLOSED state use Reset Code 3, 'No Connection', unless otherwise specified. This state has no associated sequence number variables.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Resets sent in the LISTEN state use Reset Code 3, 'No Connection', unless otherwise specified. This state has no associated sequence number variables.

statements.description: Resets sent in the TIMEWAIT state use Reset Code 3, 'No Connection', unless otherwise specified. This state has no associated sequence number variables.

actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 4 (Packet Error)

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP endpoints in CLOSED, LISTEN, or TIMEWAIT state may need to generate a DCCP-Reset packet in response to a packet received from a peer. Since these states have no associated sequence number variables, the Sequence and Acknowledgement Numbers on the DCCP-Reset packet R are taken from the received packet P.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = CLOSED | protocol.state = LISTEN | protocol.state = TIMEWAIT
actions: if P.ackno exists then set R.seqno := P.ackno + 1 else set R.seqno := 0
set R.ackno := P.seqno
if P.X = 0 then set upper 24 bits of R.seqno and R.ackno to 0
send DCCP-Reset

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP endpoints generate DCCP-Reset packets to terminate connections abnormally; a DCCP-Reset packet may be generated from any state.
actions: generate DCCP-Reset packet

statements.subject: endpoint

statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = CLOSED | protocol.state = LISTEN | protocol.state = TIMEWAIT
actions: set R.seqno := P.ackno + 1 if P.ackno exists, else R.seqno := 0
set R.ackno := P.seqno
if P.X = 0, set upper 24 bits of R.seqno and R.ackno to 0
send DCCP-Reset packet

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: Each CCID Profile document MUST address at least the following requirements:

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: The profile MUST include the name and number of the CCID being described.

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: The profile MUST describe the conditions in which it is likely to be useful.

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: The profile MUST list and describe any CCID-specific options, features, and Reset Codes and SHOULD list those general options and features described in this document that are especially relevant to the CCID.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Any newly defined acknowledgement mechanism MUST include a way to transmit ECN Nonce Echoes back to the sender.

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: The profile MUST describe the format of data packets, including any options that should be included and the setting of the CCval header field.

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: The profile MUST describe the format of acknowledgement packets, including any options that should be included.

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: The profile MUST define how data packets are congestion controlled.

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: CCIDs that implement per-packet congestion control SHOULD discuss how packet size is factored in to congestion control decisions.

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: The profile MUST specify when acknowledgement packets are generated and how they are congestion controlled.

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: The profile MUST define when a sender using the CCID is considered quiescent.

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: The profile MUST say whether its CCID's acknowledgements ever need to be acknowledged and, if so, how often.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Therefore, DCCP senders and receivers SHOULD reset their congestion state -- essentially restarting congestion control from "slow start" or equivalent -- on significant changes in the end-to-end path.
actions: reset congestion state to slow start or equivalent

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: For example, an endpoint that sends or receives a Mobile IPv6 Binding Update message [RFC3775] SHOULD reset its congestion state for any corresponding DCCP connections.
actions: reset congestion state for all corresponding DCCP connections

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A DCCP implementation MAY also reset its congestion state when a CCID changes (that is, when a negotiation for the CCID feature completes successfully and the new feature value differs from the old value).
actions: reset congestion state

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: To prevent it, DCCP implementations MAY limit the rate at which CCID can be changed -- for instance, by refusing to change a CCID feature value more than once per minute.
actions: limit rate of CCID feature value changes
optionally refuse CCID change if changed within prior minute

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP receivers MUST report all congestion they see, as defined by the relevant CCID profile.
actions: report all observed congestion as defined by the relevant CCID profile

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Acknowledgement options received on other packet types, namely DCCP-Request and DCCP-Data, MUST be ignored.
actions: ignore acknowledgement options present on DCCP-Request or DCCP-Data packets

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: DCCP was designed to work well for both bidirectional and unidirectional flows of data, and for connections that transition between these states.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP B goes 'quiescent'. This means that the connection becomes unidirectional: DCCP B stops sending data and sends only DCCP-Ack packets to DCCP A.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP A switches its ack pattern from bidirectional to unidirectional when it notices that DCCP B has gone quiescent.
actions: switch ack pattern to unidirectional

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The HC-Sender should occasionally inform the HC-Receiver that it has received an ack.
actions: send ack-of-ack to HC-Receiver

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: Therefore, the CCID in force on that half-connection must explicitly say whether, when, and how the HC-Sender should generate acks-of-acks.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP A must occasionally acknowledge a pure acknowledgement from DCCP B so that B can free old Ack Vector state.
statements.trigger: receive pure acknowledgement (DCCP-Ack) from DCCP B
actions: send acknowledgement of DCCP B's acknowledgement (ack-of-ack)

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: It switches from unidirectional to bidirectional when it must acknowledge even a single DCCP-Data or DCCP-DataAck packet from DCCP B.
statements.trigger: receive DCCP-Data or DCCP-DataAck from DCCP B
actions: switch ack pattern from unidirectional to bidirectional

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Acknowledgements of A-to-B data MAY be piggybacked on data sent by DCCP B, as long as that does not delay the acknowledgement longer than the A-to-B CCID would find acceptable.
actions: piggyback A-to-B acknowledgement onto B-to-A data packet

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: In this case, DCCP B SHOULD send separate DCCP-Data and DCCP-Ack packets, or wait, but not too long, for a smaller datagram.
statements.trigger: piggybacked acknowledgement would cause packet to exceed maximum packet size
actions: send separate DCCP-Data packet
send separate DCCP-Ack packet
OR wait briefly for a smaller datagram to piggyback onto

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Receivers MAY piggyback acknowledgement information on data packets, creating DCCP-DataAck packets.
actions: piggyback acknowledgement information on outgoing data packet
send DCCP-DataAck packet

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: However, if the data packets are too big to carry acknowledgement information, or if the data sending rate is lower than Ack Ratio would suggest, then DCCP B SHOULD send enough pure DCCP-Ack packets to maintain the rate of one acknowledgement per Ack Ratio received data packets.
actions: send pure DCCP-Ack packets at rate of one acknowledgement per Ack Ratio received data packets

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Receivers MAY rate-pace their acknowledgements rather than send acknowledgements immediately upon the receipt of data packets.
actions: rate-pace acknowledgements instead of sending immediately on receipt

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Receivers that rate-pace acknowledgements SHOULD pick a rate that approximates the effect of Ack Ratio and SHOULD include Elapsed Time options (Section 13.2) to help the sender calculate round-trip times.
actions: select acknowledgement rate approximating Ack Ratio effect
include Elapsed Time options in acknowledgement packets

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Receivers SHOULD implement delayed acknowledgement timers like TCP's, whereby any packet's acknowledgement is delayed by at most T seconds.
actions: start delayed acknowledgement timer with maximum delay T seconds
send acknowledgement when timer expires or T seconds elapsed

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Receivers SHOULD send acknowledgements immediately on receiving packets marked ECN Congestion Experienced or packets whose out-of-order sequence numbers potentially indicate loss.
actions: send acknowledgement immediately without waiting for delayed-ack timer

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Receivers MAY ignore Ack Ratio if they perform their own congestion control on acknowledgements.
actions: ignore Ack Ratio feature value for acknowledgement scheduling

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Such a receiver MUST either ensure that it always obtains sufficient acknowledgement loss and mark information or fall back to Ack Ratio when sufficient information is not available, as might happen during periods when the receiver is quiescent.
actions: ensure sufficient acknowledgement loss and mark information is continuously obtained
fall back to Ack Ratio-based scheduling when sufficient information is unavailable

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The term "ECN marked" refers to packets with ECN code point 11, CE (Congestion Experienced); packets received with this ECN code point MUST be reported using State 1, Received ECN Marked.
actions: report packet in Ack Vector using State 1 (Received ECN Marked)

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Packets received with ECN code points 00, 01, or 10 (Non-ECT, ECT(0), or ECT(1), respectively) MUST be reported using State 0, Received.
actions: report packet in Ack Vector using State 0 (Received)

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Ack Vector MUST NOT be sent on DCCP-Data and DCCP-Request packets, which lack an Acknowledgement Number, and any Ack Vector options encountered on such packets MUST be ignored.
actions: omit Ack Vector option from DCCP-Data packets
omit Ack Vector option from DCCP-Request packets

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: (These principles SHOULD also be followed for other acknowledgement mechanisms; referring to Ack Vector states simplifies their explanation.)

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Packets reported as State 0 or State 1 MUST be acknowledgeable: their options have been processed by the receiving DCCP stack.
actions: ensure options of packets reported as State 0 or State 1 have been processed by the receiving DCCP stack before reporting

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Packets reported as State 3 MUST NOT be acknowledgeable.
actions: ensure packets reported as State 3 are not acknowledged

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Feature negotiations and options on such packets MUST NOT have been processed, and the Acknowledgement Number MUST NOT correspond to such a packet.
actions: do not process feature negotiations on packets reported as State 3
do not process options on packets reported as State 3

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Packets dropped in the application's receive buffer MUST be reported as Received or Received ECN Marked (States 0 and 1), depending on their ECN state; such packets' ECN Nonces MUST be included in the Nonce Echo.
actions: report application-receive-buffer-dropped packets as State 0 (Received) or State 1 (Received ECN Marked) depending on ECN state

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: One or more Ack Vector options that, together, report the status of a packet with a sequence number less than ISN, the initial sequence number, SHOULD be considered invalid.
actions: treat Ack Vector option as invalid when it reports a sequence number less than ISN

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The receiving DCCP SHOULD either ignore the options or reset the connection with Reset Code 5, "Option Error".
actions: ignore the invalid Ack Vector options
OR send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 5 (Option Error)

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Packets that haven't been included in any Ack Vector option SHOULD be treated as "not yet received" (State 3) by the sender.
actions: treat packets not covered by any Ack Vector option as State 3 (not yet received) at the sender

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Ack Vector State 0: the packet was received and is not ECN-marked (received non-marked).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Ack Vector State 1: the packet was received and is ECN-marked (received ECN marked).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Ack Vector State 3: the packet was not received.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The HC-Receiver received packet 24 between sending its acks, so the first ack said 24 was not received (State 3) and the second said it was received or ECN marked (State 0 or 1).
actions: update Ack Vector entry to State 0

statements.description: The HC-Receiver received packet 24 between sending its acks, and the network reordered the acks. In this case, the packet will appear to transition from State 0 or 1 to State 3.
actions: update Ack Vector entry to State 3 due to reordering

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The network duplicated packet 24, and one of the duplicates was ECN marked. This might show up as a transition between States 0 and 1.
actions: update Ack Vector entry to State 1 due to ECN-marked duplicate

statements.subject: message
statements.description: HC-Sender combining table: old state 3, received state 0 yields new state 0. Allows the HC-Sender to undo its reaction to presumed congestion when a lost packet unexpectedly shows up (the transition from State 3 to State 0).
actions: combine Ack Vector states to new state 0

statements.subject: message
statements.description: HC-Sender combining table: old state 3, received state 1 yields new state 1.
actions: combine Ack Vector states to new state 1

statements.description: HC-Sender combining table: old state 1, received state 3 yields new state 1 (State 1 is sticky against State 3).
actions: retain Ack Vector state as 1

statements.subject: message
statements.description: HC-Sender combining table: old state 0, received state 3 yields new state 0 (State 0 is sticky against State 3 at sender).
actions: retain Ack Vector state as 0

statements.subject: message
statements.description: HC-Receiver stored-state table: stored state 1, received packet state 0 yields new stored state 0 or 1. The receiver is allowed to switch its stored state to 0.
actions: update stored Ack Vector state to 0

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: To cope with these situations, HC-Sender DCCP implementations SHOULD combine multiple received Ack Vector states according to this table:
actions: combine multiple received Ack Vector states according to the defined combination table

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The HC-Receiver should collect information about received packets according to the following table:

actions: set packet Ack Vector state to 0 or 1 when old state is 0 and received state is 1

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An HC-Sender MAY choose to throw away old information gleaned from the HC-Receiver's Ack Vectors, in which case it MUST ignore newly received acknowledgements from the HC-Receiver for those old packets.
actions: discard old Ack Vector information gleaned from HC-Receiver

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP A MUST send Ack Vector options on its acknowledgements when Send Ack Vector/A has value one, although it MAY send Ack Vector options even when Send Ack Vector/A is zero.
actions: include Ack Vector options on all acknowledgements

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The HC-Sender SHOULD NOT increase its sending rate for approximately one round-trip time after seeing a packet with a Slow Receiver option.
actions: do not increase sending rate for approximately one round-trip time after receiving Slow Receiver option

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: the HC-Receiver SHOULD continue to send Slow Receiver options if it needs to prevent the HC-Sender from going faster in the long term.
actions: continue sending Slow Receiver options in outgoing packets

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: One or more Data Dropped options that, together, report the status of more packets than have been sent, or that change the status of a packet, or that disagree with Ack Vector or equivalent options SHOULD be considered invalid. The receiving DCCP SHOULD either ignore such options, or respond by resetting the connection with Reset Code 5, 'Option Error'.
actions: send Reset with Reset Code 5 (Option Error)

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: Unless it is explicitly specified otherwise, DCCP congestion control mechanisms MUST react as if each Data Dropped packet was marked as ECN Congestion Experienced by the network.

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: We intend for Data Dropped to enable research into richer congestion responses to corrupt and other endpoint-dropped packets, but DCCP CCIDs MUST react conservatively to Data Dropped until this behavior is standardized.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If a received packet's application data is dropped for one of the reasons listed below, this SHOULD be reported using a Data Dropped option.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Alternatively, the receiver MAY choose to report as "received" only those packets whose data were not dropped, subject to the constraint that packets not reported as received MUST NOT have had their options processed.
actions: report as received only packets whose data were not dropped

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Data Dropped MUST NOT be sent on DCCP-Data or DCCP-Request packets, which lack an Acknowledgement Number, and any Data Dropped options received on such packets MUST be ignored.
actions: omit Data Dropped option from DCCP-Data and DCCP-Request packets

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Packets reported as "not yet received" MUST be included in Normal Blocks; packets not covered by any Data Dropped option are treated as if they were in a Normal Block.

actions: omit Data Dropped option when all relevant packets fit into Normal Blocks

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: One or more Data Dropped options that, together, report the status of more packets than have been sent, or that change the status of a packet, or that disagree with Ack Vector or equivalent options (by reporting a "not yet received" packet as "dropped in the receive buffer", for example) SHOULD be considered invalid.
actions: classify received Data Dropped options as invalid

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The receiving DCCP SHOULD either ignore such options, or respond by resetting the connection with Reset Code 5, "Option Error".
actions: ignore invalid Data Dropped options
OR send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 5 'Option Error'

statements.subject: user
statements.description: The interface SHOULD NOT let applications reduce the "seriousness" of a packet's Drop Code; for example, the application should not be able to upgrade a packet from delivered corrupt (Drop Code 7) to delivered normally (no Drop Code).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: That is, endpoints SHOULD continue to transmit Data Dropped options until receiving an acknowledgement indicating that the relevant options have been processed.
actions: retransmit Data Dropped options until acknowledgement of processing is received

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: When deciding on a response to a particular acknowledgement or set of acknowledgements containing Data Dropped options, a congestion control mechanism MUST consider dropped packets, ECN Congestion Experienced marks (including marked packets that are included in Data Dropped), and packets singled out in Data Dropped.
actions: consider dropped packets in congestion response
consider ECN Congestion Experienced marks (including marked packets included in Data Dropped) in congestion response
consider packets singled out in Data Dropped in congestion response

actions: set W_new such that W_new <= min(W_new1, W_new2)

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: Non-window-based congestion control mechanisms MUST behave analogously; again, CCID profiles define how.
actions: apply analogous combined response to dropped packets, ECN marks, and Data Dropped signals as defined by CCID profile

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Drop Code 0, Protocol Constraints, does not indicate any kind of congestion, so the sender's CCID SHOULD react to packets with Drop Code 0 as if they were received (with or without ECN Congestion Experienced marks, as appropriate).
actions: React to packet with Drop Code 0 as if it were received, with or without ECN Congestion Experienced marks as appropriate

statements.subject: endpoint

actions: Suppress data transmission until protocol constraint is believed resolved

statements.subject: endpoint

actions: Send Data Dropped option containing Drop Code 1

actions: Report Drop Code 1 for every succeeding data packet on that half-connection

Stop sending data on that half-connection

actions: Reduce sender instantaneous rate by one packet per round-trip time

statements.subject: dccp

actions: Cause relevant CCID to behave as if relevant packets were ECN Congestion Experienced marked

actions: set ECN-Capable Transport on outgoing packet IP headers

statements.subject: connection

statements.description: Each DCCP sender SHOULD set ECN Nonces on its packets and remember which packets had nonces.

statements.description: Each DCCP receiver MUST calculate and use the correct value for ECN Nonce Echo when sending acknowledgement options.
